title: Dive into Time-Series Anomaly Detection: A Decade Review
authors: Boniol, P.; Liu, Q.; Huang, M.; Palpanas, T.; Paparrizos, J.
tldr: Comprehensive survey of time-series anomaly detection methods organized under a process-centric taxonomy covering distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based approaches over a decade of research.
problem_and_motivation: Time-series anomaly detection has grown rapidly across cybersecurity, finance, healthcare, and other domains, yet existing surveys focus on general-purpose anomaly detection and only briefly review time-series-specific methods. The field remains fragmented, with different communities using different datasets, baselines, and evaluation measures, making it virtually impossible to identify the best state-of-the-art approach for a concrete use case.
approach: A process-centric taxonomy is proposed grouping anomaly detection methods into distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based categories with nine second-level subcategories.
Distance-based methods are subdivided into proximity-based, clustering-based, and discord-based approaches that detect anomalies using raw time-series distances.
Density-based methods process time-series data on complex representations including distributions, graphs, trees, and encodings to measure point or sub-sequence density.
Prediction-based methods are split into forecasting-based and reconstruction-based approaches that use prediction or reconstruction error as the anomaly score.
A meta-analysis examines research trends over time, revealing a significant increase in methods after 2016 driven primarily by LSTM and autoencoder-based approaches.
Existing benchmarks including NAB, Yahoo, Exathlon, KDD21, TODS, TimeEval, TSB-UAD, and TSB-AD are catalogued and compared.
Evaluation measures are categorized into threshold-based and threshold-independent types, with VUS-ROC recommended as the most robust metric.
findings: Between 2020 and 2023, LSTM and autoencoder-based approaches represent almost 50 percent of newly introduced anomaly detection methods.
65 percent of anomaly detection methods proposed between 1980 and 2000 were unsupervised, whereas 50 percent of methods proposed between 2012 and 2018 were unsupervised.
Most methods proposed before 2016 were designed for point anomaly detection in multivariate time series, while recent methods increasingly target univariate sub-sequence anomalies.
Simple time-series classification baselines can improve accuracy by a factor of 2 compared to the best performing individual anomaly detection method through model selection.
TSB-AD is the largest benchmark with 1,000 curated time-series datasets benchmarking 40 anomaly detection approaches.

key_equations.explanation: K-th nearest neighbor anomaly score using aggregation of distances to k neighbors.
Local Outlier Factor comparing local reachability density of neighbors.
Isolation Forest anomaly score based on average path length to isolation.

definitions.definition: A single data point that deviates remarkably from the rest of the data distribution.
A data point within the expected global range but abnormal given its local context or window.
A sequence of points that collectively do not repeat an expected previously observed pattern.
A sub-sequence whose distance to its nearest neighbor is the largest among all sub-sequences.
A metadata time series where each element is the Euclidean distance of a sub-sequence to its nearest neighbor.
Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms for learning long-term dependencies in sequences.
A neural network that learns to compress input into a latent space and reconstruct it, using reconstruction error for anomaly scoring.
Generative Adversarial Network with a generator and discriminator trained adversarially to detect anomalies.
Volume Under the Surface, a threshold-independent evaluation metric computing Range-AUC across multiple buffer lengths.
An anomaly detection method that isolates anomalies by random partitioning, with anomalies requiring fewer partitions to isolate.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides a comprehensive, process-centric taxonomy of time-series anomaly detection methods organized into distance-based, density-based, and prediction-based categories with nine subcategories. It catalogs over a hundred methods spanning four decades of research, from early statistical approaches to modern deep learning techniques. The paper also conducts a meta-analysis revealing key research trends, including the shift toward deep learning after 2016 and the growing interest in univariate sub-sequence detection. Additionally, it critically evaluates existing benchmarks and proposes VUS-ROC as a robust evaluation metric.
limits: The taxonomy does not include personal finance or budgeting applications.
The benchmarking discussion focuses on general anomaly detection rather than financial transaction data.
The survey does not address user-facing deployment or mobile integration concerns.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. This paper is a general survey of time-series anomaly detection methods and does not address personal finance systems, budgeting, expense categorization, user behavior profiling, or any other domain-specific topic in the taxonomy. The anomaly detection algorithms discussed (LSTM, Isolation Forest, Autoencoders) are general-purpose and not evaluated on personal spending data. No topic codes from the personal finance taxonomy apply, as the paper's contributions lie entirely in the general time-series mining research domain.

limitations: The survey focuses on general-purpose time-series anomaly detection without addressing domain-specific adaptations for personal finance.
Most benchmarks reviewed contain synthetic or industrial data rather than real-world personal financial transaction data.
The rapid growth of methods after 2016 makes it challenging to keep the taxonomy current as new approaches emerge.
The survey does not address streaming or real-time deployment constraints relevant to mobile personal finance applications.
remember_this: The survey proposes a three-tier process-centric taxonomy with nine subcategories for time-series anomaly detection methods.
LSTM and autoencoder approaches dominate recent research, accounting for nearly 50 percent of new methods from 2020 to 2023.
VUS-ROC is recommended as the most robust threshold-independent evaluation metric for time-series anomaly detection.
No single anomaly detector performs best across all datasets, motivating research into model selection and ensembling.
